title: 〜どころか
meaning: far from… / let alone… / not only not… but actually…
simpleExplanation: 〜どころか means "far from (X), actually (Y)". You mention what someone might expect (X) and then knock it down: the reality is completely different, often the opposite. It has two flavours: (1) "far from X, it's the opposite" (楽になるどころか、忙しくなった), and (2) "not even the easy thing, let alone the hard one" (漢字どころか、ひらがなも読めない).
whenUsed: Spoken and written, fairly emphatic. Used when correcting expectations strongly, complaining, or being surprised. Because it is emphatic, it is not used in polite apologies or neutral reports.
formation: な-adjective (stem) + どころか  (or + な + どころか)
Second clause often contains 〜も〜ない (not even…) or the opposite of the first clause

diagram.title: Two uses of どころか

rows.label: Opposite result
cells: X どころか、(opposite of X)
薬を飲んだら、よくなるどころか、悪くなった
Far from getting better after taking the medicine, I got worse.

rows.label: Not even the easy thing
cells: 漢字どころか、ひらがなも書けない
He can't even write hiragana, let alone kanji.

examples.ja: 薬を飲んだら、よくなるどころか、かえって悪くなった。
examples.reading: くすりをのんだら、よくなるどころか、かえってわるくなった。
examples.en: Far from getting better after taking the medicine, I actually got worse.
examples.note: かえって (on the contrary) reinforces the reversal.

examples.ja: 彼は漢字どころか、ひらがなも読めない。
examples.reading: かれはかんじどころか、ひらがなもよめない。
examples.en: He can't even read hiragana, let alone kanji.
examples.note: Noun + どころか + easy thing + も + negative.

examples.ja: 今年の夏は涼しいどころか、記録的な暑さだった。
examples.reading: ことしのなつはすずしいどころか、きろくてきなあつさだった。
examples.en: This summer was far from cool; it was record-breaking heat.

examples.ja: 休みの日はゆっくりするどころか、家事で一日中動き回っている。
examples.reading: やすみのひはゆっくりするどころか、かじでいちにちじゅううごきまわっている。
examples.en: On my days off, far from relaxing, I'm running around doing housework all day.

examples.ja: あの店は安いどころか、他の店の倍の値段だった。
examples.reading: あのみせはやすいどころか、ほかのみせのばいのねだんだった。
examples.en: That shop wasn't cheap at all; the prices were double other shops'.

similarGrammar.difference: "This is no time/situation for X" – the speaker is too busy or troubled. どころか compares two things.
"Not only X but also Y", where X and Y point in the same direction. どころか reverses direction.
"Not to mention" – both items are true. With どころか, the first item is denied.
"Not limited to" – neutral addition, no reversal.

commonMistakes.wrong: 彼は英語どころか、フランス語も話せる。
commonMistakes.right: 彼は英語ばかりか、フランス語も話せる。
commonMistakes.why: Both items are positive (he can speak both), so the pattern is ばかりか. どころか requires the first item to be denied or reversed.

commonMistakes.wrong: 忙しくて、旅行どころか。
commonMistakes.right: 忙しくて、旅行どころではない。
commonMistakes.why: "I'm too busy for a trip" is どころではない. どころか must be followed by a second clause.

commonMistakes.wrong: ひらがなどころか、漢字も読めない。
commonMistakes.right: 漢字どころか、ひらがなも読めない。
commonMistakes.why: With "let alone", the harder thing comes first (漢字), then the easier thing with も + negative (ひらがなも).

usageNotes: The second clause frequently contains かえって, 逆に, or まったく to emphasize the reversal.
In the "let alone" use, the order is: bigger/harder thing + どころか + smaller/easier thing + も/さえ + negative.
どころか can also start a sentence as a rebuttal: それどころか (on the contrary…).
jlptTips: In 文法形式の判断, if the second clause is the opposite of the first or a "not even…" statement, どころか is the answer. If the second clause simply adds another positive item, it is ばかりか.
Common distractors: どころではない, ばかりか, はもちろん, ものの. Check the direction of the two clauses.
In 並べ替え, どころか is usually the second chunk; find the clause that gets denied and place it before どころか.
